elements.element: The Vendor must maintain commercial general liability insurance with a limit of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The added clause contains no commercial general liability insurance requirement.

elements.element: The Vendor must maintain commercial general liability insurance with an aggregate limit of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The added clause contains no commercial general liability aggregate limit.

elements.element: The Vendor must maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 10.14 requires professional liability insurance of only USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: If the Vendor processes Customer Data, the Vendor must maintain cyber and privacy liability insurance of at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: The condition is not demonstrably absent, and Section 10.14 requires cyber and privacy liability insurance of only USD 2,000,000.

elements.element: The Vendor must maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
elements.evidence: The added clause contains no workers' compensation insurance requirement.

elements.element: The Vendor must provide certificates of insurance upon request.
elements.evidence: The added clause contains no obligation to provide certificates of insurance.

elements.element: The Vendor must maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 10.14 requires the Servicer to maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: The Vendor must maintain cyber and privacy liability insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 10.14 requires the Servicer to maintain cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000.

result.reason: The operative addition fully reaches the stated fallback by imposing the required E&O and cyber/privacy insurance limits on the Servicer. It does not reach the preferred position because it omits commercial general liability, workers' compensation, and certificates-on-request requirements and uses lower E&O and cyber/privacy limits. The addition is confined to the fallback insurance covenant and does not contradict the surrounding receivables provisions.
